# OCSL freeze-gated tables -- format 1
#
# GENERATED by OcslTablesGenerator. Do not hand-edit: regenerate and read the
# diff. Every line is a FROZEN CONTRACT a saved blob depends on, not an
# observation of what the code happens to do. A register id that moves
# invalidates every blob written under the old number; a charge that moves
# moves all four committed acceptance counts.
#
# This file freezes the three tables the roadmap gates the format freeze on:
# per-surface register ids, constructor arity, and op accounting. It exists
# because the design document cannot serve the role -- docs/ is gitignored and
# does not ship.
#
# IT IS NOT A COMPLETE FORMAT SPECIFICATION, and the first cut of this header
# said it was. An adversarial pass applied seven format-breaking mutations at
# once -- a colliding built-in id, PROP_COLOR renumbered, the operand tag bit
# moved, swizzle packing changed, MAX made strict instead of broadcasting, the
# input sampler extended to bake, a readable register added to the vertex stage
# -- and this file rendered BYTE-IDENTICAL to all of them. Four of those are now
# covered; the rest are listed under [not-frozen-here] at the end, because a
# frozen artifact that overstates its coverage is worse than none.
#
#   ./gradlew ocslTables    regenerate

[stages] material=1 effect=2 post=3 bake=4 vertex=5 animator=6 compute=7
# The stage byte a blob carries. Absent from the first cut of this file, which
# made it impossible to decode a blob's stage field from the table alone.

[open] stage open composes
# Whether a program may be built, validated or run on this surface at all.
# SEPARATE from whether it mandates an output -- see [properties] required. The
# animator is the surface that distinguishes them, and since 2026-08-13 it does so
# by EXAMPLE rather than by prediction: it is open AND mandates nothing, a pair the
# single coupled predicate could not represent. Its required set must stay empty.
# composes: whether output values compose over a server-set base. It gates the
# absolute output form -- OUT_ABS is refused where this is no, because a stage
# whose output IS the value has no base to replace and would gain a second
# spelling for one behaviour. Independent of `open` -- the animator composes and
# the pixel family does not, while both are open -- which is why the two columns
# exist rather than one.
material yes no
effect yes no
post yes no
bake yes no
vertex no no
animator yes yes
compute no no

[properties] stage id name type required
# What OUT's `property` operand means, in the stage's OWN namespace.
# required: the stage refuses a program that does not write it.
material 0 COLOR vec4 yes
effect 0 COLOR vec4 yes
post 0 COLOR vec4 yes
bake 0 COLOR vec4 yes
animator 0 x float no
animator 1 y float no
animator 2 sx float no
animator 3 sy float no
animator 4 rot2d float no
animator 5 rot3d vec4 no
animator 6 tint vec4 no
animator 9 tz float no
animator 10 sz float no
# Animator ids with NO row are reserved without a type, deliberately: `z` (int)
# and `visible` (bool) are not ownable in v1 -- neither interpolates, and IR bool
# is conditions-only -- so their ids are held but no OUT may target them.
animator 7 z reserved no
animator 8 visible reserved no

[time] name value
# The `time` production (ANIM-4) and the wrap period P (ANIM-5). Unlike every id
# in this file, P is NOT encoded in a blob -- it is supplied at runtime through
# the timePeriod register, so moving it costs no format bump.
tickNanos 50000000
periodTicks 33600
periodNanos 1680000000000
periodSecondsBits 0x44D20000
unit seconds
clock render
domain half-open-0-to-P
producers 1

[composition] property rule identity own-read reg
# How an animator's output combines with the server-set base WHEN THE PROGRAM
# USED THE RELATIVE FORM, `OUT`. The rule below is the DEFAULT, not the whole
# story: an `OUT_ABS` write (opcode 81, see [ops]) means disp=out for any
# property, whatever its row here says, and one writer per property covers both
# forms together. A backend implementing this section alone would apply the base
# twice to every absolute write. add: disp=srv+out.
# mul: disp=srv*out. replace: disp=out. quat: disp=q_srv*q_out normalized,
# animator-local applied FIRST, components (x,y,z) vector and w scalar.
# x and y compose IN THE PARENT'S FRAME -- they are NOT rotated by the server
# transform. The base is narrowed to float32 BEFORE composing, so the result is a
# pure function of what the VM saw and two clients cannot disagree on it.
#
# own-read: ANIM-7's double-apply rule. `forfeited` means a program writing this
# property with the RELATIVE form may not read the register in the last column --
# that write already composes over it, so building on it applies the base twice,
# and the read is refused at validate. `kept` means the read stays legal, which
# is exactly the REPLACE properties: the base never enters an accepted result
# there, so doubling is arithmetically impossible. OUT_ABS may always read it.
# reg is the property's own raw read register, and it is NOT base+id: z and
# visible hold property ids with no register, so tz and sz sit two below where
# arithmetic would put them.
x add 0 forfeited 16
y add 0 forfeited 17
sx mul 1 forfeited 18
sy mul 1 forfeited 19
rot2d add 0 forfeited 20
rot3d quat 0,0,0,1 forfeited 21
tint replace none kept 22
tz add 0 forfeited 23
sz mul 1 forfeited 24
# `none` is not an omission: tint REPLACES, so no output leaves the base alone.

[ingress] site remedy
# What happens to a value on its way IN. The rule binds EVERY stage, animator and
# bake included. It was written under a 'non-finite values at the PIXEL STAGE'
# heading whose own back-reference pointed at the WRITE rule, so nothing in the
# design said so; every method on OcslIngress now takes no stage, which is the
# enforced spelling of that sentence.
constantPool refuse-the-program
registerBinding substitute-zero
animatorScalarBase substitute-composition-identity
animatorTintBase substitute-white
animatorRot3dBase substitute-identity-quaternion
uniformSetCall not-implemented
# Zero is the remedy for a BINDING and the wrong one for a BASE: a non-finite base
# reaches an op, A4's catch-all zeroes the whole result, and mul(NaN,2) is 0 -- so a
# multiplicative property collapses the node. The identity is what leaves the other
# side intact, and it is the mirror of a rejected output falling back to the base.
# The set-call may reject-and-retain because the uniform table is REPLICATED and the
# retained value is then identical on every client. The executor may NOT: a frame is
# per-client, so a retained value there is binding history -- the cross-frame state
# ANIM-9(a) removed. No host-facing setUniform exists YET -- and the reason given
# here until 2026-08-23 was false: it said nothing in the running mod creates or
# attaches a program. TileEntityGpu2 has both createProgram and setAnimator, so a
# player CAN declare a uniform and attach the program; it then evaluates against a
# zero frame with no refusal. A diagnostic shipped in the same commit that
# wrote this line (67b3bf8, 2026-08-24): a counter, an overlay row, one log
# line -- the VALUE is still 0.0, only the silence was fixed. That row is a
# stated gap rather than an omission, but it is a REACHABLE one.

[write-boundary] name value
# What happens to a value on its way out. A non-finite animator output is
# REJECTED and the frame displays the server base -- statelessly, by substituting
# the property's identity, so a client that joined on the failing frame and one
# that watched for a minute agree. The superseded 'previous value retained' rule
# was the only cross-frame state in the design and the one place purity broke.
# Finite out-of-range is CLAMPED, not rejected: it still carries intent.
nonFinitePolicy reject-to-server-base
rot3dReject identity-quaternion
# rot3d gets its own row because identityFor THROWS for a quaternion, so the scalar
# path could not express 'falls back to the server base' and did not: a non-finite
# animator quaternion used to fall out of the norm guard as the identity ROTATION,
# discarding q_srv too, and a node with a server rotation snapped upright.
trsLimit 1000000.0
colorClamp 0..1
colorSteps 255
colorRounding half-up
colorOrder clamp-then-quantize
# clamp-then-quantize is load-bearing, not a preference: the destination is a
# packed 8-bit-per-channel int that does NOT saturate. (int)(1.5*255) is 382,
# which is 0x17E, and shifted into the alpha byte it lands as 126 -- a dark flash
# where the author asked for full brightness.

[diagnostics] name value
# 'Logged once per program' was the wrong unit. A curated preset is one program
# id across many nodes, so the first failing node consumed the only line and every
# other node's failure was invisible for the session -- the opposite of what a
# diagnostic is for. Both halves of the key are compared exactly: folding them
# into one number would let a collision suppress a distinct node while looking
# exactly like correct deduplication.
unit program+node
burst 16
refillNanos 10000000000
maxTracked 256
onTableFull clear-and-allow-repeats
order rate-check-before-record
# order is a rule, not an implementation detail: recording first would let a
# scene-load burst consume dedup slots for pairs that never produced a line, and
# those failures would then be silent forever.

[slots] name value
# Sampler bindings are their own namespace, not registers.
inputSlot 0
inputSamplerStages effect,post

[stage-caps] stage fetches uniformComponents
# fetches 0 at the animator is a RULE: no sampler exists in its register set, so
# a fetch names a resource the surface cannot bind. The 64-component uniform
# budget is the GL floor and does not apply where nothing is lowered to GLSL;
# the animator is bounded by the frame-width cap instead. Node property input
# registers do NOT charge against either -- they are built-ins, not declarations.
material 16 64
effect 16 64
post 16 64
bake 16 64
vertex 16 64
animator 0 64
compute 16 64

[constructors] op operands result charge
# The shapes amendment 4 pins. `f` is a float operand, `vN` a vector of width N.
SPLAT f+width v2..v4 1
CONS2 f,f v2 1
CONS3 f,f,f v3 1
CONS4 f,f,f,f v4 1
CONS3_V2F v2,f v3 1
CONS4_V3F v3,f v4 1
CONS4_V2V2 v2,v2 v4 1
# SWZ is not a constructor: it selects 1..4 components from an existing value and
# its result width is the swizzle length, so it carries no fixed arity row.

[ops] opcode name charge dst kinds
# charge: structural ops debited per EXECUTION (post-unroll). dst: does it write
# a register. kinds: operand slots -- value/imm/property/slot/swizzle.

45 CONS3_V2F 1 dst value,value

50 LT 1 dst value,value

[blocks] name base limit
# Half-open [base, limit). Claimed now, assigned later.
light 10 16
animator 16 48
uniform 48 112
working 112 1024

[caps] name value
# Most of these may be RAISED under the monotonicity rule and never lowered once
# blobs exist. TWO EXCEPTIONS, because the blanket claim was wrong:
#   maxUniforms  CANNOT be raised. It is uniformLimit - uniformBase, and
#                uniformLimit == workingBase, so raising it either overlaps the
#                working block or moves workingBase -- which renumbers every
#                working register in every saved blob. Raising it is a format
#                break, not a relaxation.
#   maxRegisters may be raised only to the DECODER's own separate bound, which
#                is not this number and is not in this file. Same simple name,
#                different constant.
maxRegisters 1024
maxFrameWidth 2048
maxSlots 16
maxUniforms 64
maxStructuralOps 8192
maxStructuralOps.stage1 256
maxStructuralOps.stage2 256
maxStructuralOps.stage3 256
maxStructuralOps.stage4 256
maxStructuralOps.stage5 256
maxStructuralOps.stage6 512
maxStructuralOps.stage7 256
maxFetches 16
maxUnrollProduct 8192
maxUniformComponents 64
[not-frozen-here] contract where-it-lives
# Proved absent by mutation: each of these can change while this file renders
# byte-identical. Do not read a silent diff as coverage.
operand-tag-bit OcslWire.OPERAND_CONST_FLAG/OPERAND_INDEX_MASK
swizzle-packing OcslWire.packSwizzle/swizzleComponent/swizzleLength
broadcast-vs-strict IrValidator -- which ops broadcast a float operand
splat-is-forbidden-where-broadcast-works IrValidator (forks the content hash)
result-types-per-op [ops] carries no result column; LT and SUB render alike
constructor-operand-ORDER [constructors] operand strings are literals, not derived
decoder-caps OcslWire MAX_CONSTANTS/MAX_OPS/MAX_NAMES/MAX_BLOB_BYTES/etc
blob-envelope OcslWire MAGIC/FORMAT_VERSION/TRAILING_GUARD
uniform-binding-rule declaration order from uniformBase, all float in v1
numeric-domain golden-vectors.txt (frozen there, deliberately not duplicated)
#
# `isOpen-independence` WAS on this list and came off it on 2026-08-13, which is
# the one entry here that has ever been discharged rather than deferred. It read
# 'NOT behaviourally detectable': `isOpen` and `requiredProperties(s).length != 0`
# returned the same answer for all 256 stage bytes, so re-deriving one from the
# other was a source-level regression no test and no frozen byte could catch. The
# note said it mattered 'the day the animator opens', and that day came: the
# animator is open with an EMPTY required set, so the two predicates now disagree
# on stage 6 and the [open] column above is the frozen byte that shows it.
# Re-coupling them would put back the trap the split removed -- clearing the
# validator gate by giving the animator a required property, which forces every
# animator program to own it (ANIM-2) -- and it now fails a test instead of
# passing silently. If you are here to de-duplicate those two switches: don't.
